summary: Ephemeral batch workers fail authorization after IdP group-normalizer regex change
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that scheduled batch inference jobs started failing with 403 Authorization errors for ephemeral worker pods created after a config change on 2026-03-09. Failures began at ~09:10 UTC and affected all new workers; previously-provisioned long-running workers continued to operate normally.

Impact:
- Nimbus Analytics: recurring scheduled inference jobs (nightly batch) failing end-to-end, causing missed SLAs for data pipeline deliveries.
- Errors observed from worker -> /v1/infer requests: 403 with 'role binding not found' message.
- Estimated affected job runs: 42 in the first 3 hours.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) in us-west-2.
- Redwood Private control plane version: 2026.02.28.
- IdP: On-prem SAML (Shibboleth 3.5), group claim named 'memberOf'.
- RBAC: claim-to-group mapping using idp-mapper 'group_normalizer' regex.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a new ephemeral worker via Nimbus scheduled job (same job definition as customer).
2) Observe worker pod logs showing successful token exchange with auth proxy.
3) Worker requests /v1/infer/* and receives 403 'no role binding for group: team' instead of expected 'worker' role.
4) Inspect idp-mapper output: groups emitted to Redwood are truncated to the first colon-separated segment.

Observed logs/snippets:
- auth-proxy: "token-issue: svcacct-ephemeral-123 accepted, groups=[team, infra, admins]"
- worker: "POST /v1/infer -> 403 {\"error\":\"role binding not found for groups: [team]\"}"
- idp-mapper debug: "raw memberOf: team:nimbus:workers, normalized: team"

Initial hypothesis: The group_normalizer regex was changed in the customer idp-mapper config during a maintenance change on 2026-03-09 to a simplifying pattern that strips everything after the first colon. This normalization removes tenant and role segments from namespace-qualified groups, so expected group 'nimbus:workers' (or 'team:nimbus:workers') no longer matches RBAC group patterns used by role bindings. Existing long-lived workers created before the change retained cached bindings and continued to function.

Customer-provided attachments: SAML assertion sample (redacted), worker pod logs, scheduled job run IDs.

Required next steps: immediate mitigation to restore batch jobs, followed by a configuration fix and a small code guard to prevent accidental destructive regex changes in idp-mapper.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Priya Shah (CS): Received initial report from Nimbus Support lead. Requested SAML assertion samples and job IDs.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Nimbus (customer): Provided redacted assertion and sample pod logs. Noted that rolling back worker image didn't help; only pre-existing jobs succeeded.

2026-03-10 11:20 UTC - Luca Martinez (Support/Eng): Reproduced in staging by applying the customer's group_normalizer. Confirmed truncation behavior in idp-mapper. Filed INT-88923 to track internal rollback test.

2026-03-10 13:02 UTC - SRE (oncall): Applied customer-visible mitigation: added a temporary translation table at auth-proxy to map 'team' -> 'nimbus:workers' for Nimbus tenant, restoring scheduled jobs immediately.
2026-03-11 08:30 UTC - Priya Shah (CS): Customer confirmed nightly job run succeeded after mitigation. Requested permanent fix and checklist to prevent recurrence.

2026-03-12 14:15 UTC - Luca Martinez (Eng): Merged PR to idp-mapper to make regex changes require review and to add safe-default tests. CR deployed to control plane in canary and then rolled to prod for Nimbus tenant. Marking ticket resolved.
investigation_notes: Reproduced locally: apply regex '^([^:]+):.*$' to incoming 'memberOf' claim yields single-segment group names. Expected regex should capture tenant+role segments or preserve the last segment for role mapping.
Role-binding lookup in RBAC uses pattern 'nimbus:workers' and 'team:nimbus:workers' in different customers. The normalization removed the matching substring causing lookup to fail.
Cached role-bindings on long-lived workers prevented immediate failure; ephemeral workers always perform fresh token validation and therefore failed after change.
Auth-proxy logs show token exchange succeeded but downstream request-level authorization failed since token lacked expected group names understood by RBAC engine.
Quick mitigation implemented at auth-proxy via tenant-specific header translation. This is not ideal long-term because it masks normalization errors.
Root cause: idp-mapper configuration change without schema validation and insufficient unit tests for group normalization patterns.
resolution: Applied tenant-specific translation at auth-proxy to restore Nimbus batch jobs (temporary). Rolled back the customer-provided idp-mapper regex change in the control plane for Nimbus tenant and deployed a safer mapping implementation with explicit capture groups and unit tests (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/idp-mapper/pull/432). Added a validation step in the idp-mapper UI to warn on regexes that reduce group namespace segments. Customer confirmed nightly batch run success. Follow-ups: (1) Add automated canary checks for idp-mapper changes, (2) Publish runbook entry to surface group normalization effects to customers, (3) Offer migration assistance to other private customers who may have similar regexes.
